summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found one unusually direct US-listed substrate candidate, AXT Inc., plus a small set of downstream optical module/component leaders and one equipment-enabled expansion candidate. The strongest node fit is AXTI because the external context and recent search results point to indium phosphide substrates as a scarce upstream input for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers. COHR and AAOI are included as direct product/customer anchors for 800G/1.6T transceiver demand. VECO is included as an underfollowed second-order tool supplier candidate tied to compound-semiconductor and photonics capacity expansion, but its specific linkage to the substrate chokepoint needs verification. Layer 1B expansion for the optical-transceiver substrate chokepoint points first to indium phosphide and adjacent compound-semiconductor photonics capacity. The strongest underfollowed US-listed candidate is AXT, which directly manufactures InP/GaAs/Ge compound semiconductor substrates used in optoelectronic devices and data-center connectivity. Veeco is a second-order equipment candidate because its MOCVD systems enable InP epitaxy for optical-communications lasers. Lumentum and Coherent are higher-attention reference/component anchors: they sit closer to EML/CW laser and InP photodiode demand that pulls on substrate and epitaxy capacity. Applied Optoelectronics would also be a valid downstream demand validator, but this pass limits candidates to four and prioritizes scarce inputs, tools, and component nodes over module assemblers.
